offences.quote: Plagiarism: The act of using ideas, words, or creations from either humans or digital systems, such as Generative Artificial intelligence, without proper attribution or permission and presenting them, either intentionally or unwittingly, as one’s own work.
The use of content generated by AI and failing to acknowledge this contribution with referencing and quotations.

It also includes instances of close paraphrasing, minimal adaptation, and other actions that involve reproducing the work of another source in a way that means the assessed work lacks appropriate originality or proper referencing.
Self-plagiarism: re-using work that has previously submitted for a different assessment, either at The University of Manchester or a different institution, without appropriate citation.
Collusion: when a student or students permit or condone another student or students, to share a piece of work subject to assessment in order to gain a mark or grade to which they are not entitled.

Fabrication or falsification of results, figures or data: the presentation or inclusion in a piece of work, by individual students or groups of students, of figures or any data (quantitative or qualitative) which have been made up or altered
Examination malpractice: when a student, during an examination, intentionally or unwittingly contravenes set exam conditions
sitting or allowing someone to sit an examination in place of the student supposed to be taking the examination
Contract cheating: the commissioning of a piece of work by a third party, beyond basic proofreading.

liability.quote: Academic malpractice can result from a deliberate act of cheating or may be committed unintentionally. Whether intended or not, all incidents of academic malpractice will be treated seriously by the University.

definitions.quote: Academic malpractice is any attempt (intentional or otherwise) to gain, or assist others to gain, an unfair academic advantage in academic work or research.

Plagiarism: The act of using ideas, words, or creations from either humans or digital systems, such as Generative Artificial intelligence, without proper attribution or permission and presenting them, either intentionally or unwittingly, as one’s own work.
Self-plagiarism: re-using work that has previously submitted for a different assessment, either at The University of Manchester or a different institution, without appropriate citation.

Fabrication or falsification of results, figures or data: the presentation or inclusion in a piece of work, by individual students or groups of students, of figures or any data (quantitative or qualitative) which have been made up or altered
Examination malpractice: when a student, during an examination, intentionally or unwittingly contravenes set exam conditions

Poor academic practice involves minor infringement of examination conditions or accepted citation practice
